q: How do I count catered staff meals and canteen food in our carbon footprint?
title: Staff canteen meals in your footprint
short: Food your caterer serves to staff is Scope 3 Category 1, purchased goods and services. Count meals served by menu type and multiply by a per meal factor, or, if you only have the caterer's invoices, multiply spend by a food services factor and label it spend-based. Meat and dairy dishes drive most of the result.
audience: Offices and factories with outsourced canteens

ul: Food and the caterer's service: Scope 3 Category 1.
Kitchen LPG or PNG: Scope 1 if your company buys the fuel and runs the kitchen; Category 1 inside the caterer's charge if the caterer buys it.
Kitchen electricity on your meter: Scope 2.
Food waste you send for disposal: Category 5, waste generated in operations.
Meals bought by staff with their own money in a food court: outside your inventory.

sections.h: Activity method: meals by menu type
p: Ask the caterer for monthly counts of meals served, split at least into vegetarian and non-vegetarian, and ideally by dish type. Multiply each count by a per meal factor from a published food footprint dataset and name it. Dairy heavy meals such as paneer and ghee dishes sit between plain vegetarian and meat meals, so a two-way split is the minimum, not the ideal.

If meal counts are not available, multiply the caterer's invoice value, net of GST, by a food services spend factor in kg CO2e per rupee. Convert any factor published in another currency and year to rupees for the same year. Label the result spend-based: it cannot show a menu change, and it moves with prices rather than food.

sections.h: Is it worth counting at all
p: Check it against your other categories with a quick spend estimate first. If it is material, move to meal counts so a menu change, such as more vegetarian days, shows in the number. In the example below, moving from 70% to 80% vegetarian meals cuts about 19 tonnes, which a spend figure would not show.

example.title: Illustrative example: one office canteen for a year
lines: Meals served: 500 a day x 250 working days = 125,000 meals; 70% vegetarian, 30% non-vegetarian
Vegetarian: 87,500 x 1.0 kg CO2e per meal (assumed) = 87,500 kg CO2e
Non-vegetarian: 37,500 x 2.5 kg CO2e per meal (assumed) = 93,750 kg CO2e
Total: 87,500 + 93,750 = 181,250 kg CO2e, about 181 tonnes in Category 1
Shifting to 80% vegetarian: 100,000 x 1.0 + 25,000 x 2.5 = 162,500 kg CO2e, about 19 tonnes lower
example.note: Per meal factors here are placeholders to show the method; use a named dataset and keep it fixed year to year.

senseible: Senseible reads caterer and food purchase invoices, uses printed quantities where they exist, and gives a spend-based estimate, labelled spend-based with wider uncertainty, where only spend is available. It also reads kitchen LPG invoices at 2.98 kg CO2 per kg (IPCC 2006 default) into Scope 1.
